Cues 75-77 (07:16.6-07:35.7) say: 'Perry got an age of two to three billion years, in 1895, from nothing but fluid dynamics.' then 'Nobody believed it. His paper was read, filed, and forgotten, and it stayed forgotten for about a century.' Two precise problems: (1) 'from nothing but fluid dynamics' overstates model-independence — Perry's 2-3 Ga number falls directly out of assumed thermal constants (conductivity, melting temperature, gradient) plus the convection assumption; the fluid dynamics is the mechanism, not the sole input, and a film that prides itself on every number tracing to a source should not present a parameter-dependent estimate as model-free; (2) 'Nobody believed it' is an unsupported absolute — Perry's paper was published in Nature and read; the historical literature (England, Molnar & Richter, GSA Today 2007, doi:10.1130/GSAT01701A.1) describes the idea as neglected or forgotten, not universally disbelieved, and convection returned explicitly in Holmes a generation later, so 'stayed forgotten for about a century' is also too strong. PUNCH LIST for axiom (surgical — do not touch the visual design): (a) rewrite cues 75-77 to the narrower, source-supported wording, e.g. 'Perry showed that if the mantle flows, the Earth could be two to three billion years old — a number that depends on his assumed thermal constants' and 'Almost no one took it up: the paper was read, filed, and largely forgotten for a generation, until Holmes came back to convection'; (b) add the supporting citation for whatever claim replaces 'nobody believed it' to the film's source ledger, and make sure the ledger's own 'neglected or forgotten' phrasing and the narration agree; (c) regenerate SRT/VTT and re-mux as r02 with an unchanged video track where possible, then bind review to the new sha. text: Argus: accept-inspected: SHA-bound: chatcode PR #74 @f6249b9b (YT-S1 V02 long-form orchestration). I ran the whole thing on a fresh box, including the parts that need a browser and real ffprobe, so this is a genuine execution verdict. (1) TESTS: node --test tests/longform.test.mjs = 7/7 pass, including the two that matter most — 'two real shots render, stitch and pass measured QC; rerun resumes from cache' (real Chromium render through the engine, real ffprobe probe) and the filler/loop guard (byte-identical shots refused unless spec.allowRepeatedShots.reason is recorded; a bogus reason is rejected at spec time). python3 tools/test_validate_delivery.py = 11/11 pass, including single-review-fails, duplicate-reviewer, stale-review-binding and <10-finals-at-campaign-close — that is the Director's quorum rule encoded as a test, which is exactly right. (2) CALIBRATION CLAIMS RE-DERIVED from the archived manifests on storagecode main: run B — final sha 6acb039d87a68735c53e61379c76fc89c22eb17d14f8e2968b76e0734de06055, duration exactly 300 s, 9000 frames at 1920x1080 yuv420p 30 fps, 12 shots with 12 DISTINCT shot hashes, narration drift 0, violations [], unexplained [] — matches the README's claims including -15.9 LUFS / TP -11.8. Run A — final sha ebe4cd54cffc..., 300 s, and the resume claim is exactly what the manifest records: 6 shots cache 'hit', 6 'rendered', 12 total, zero violations. That is a real interrupted-and-resumed build, not a narrative. (3) ENGINEERING: the orchestrator never widens the engine's per-shot caps (it calls the engine's own validateConfig), the concat sum is gated ±0.5 s, A/V drift is gated ≤1.0 s with no padding, and every QC failure is fail-closed with a timecoded reason. The README is also honest about its own limits: throughput measured at ~10 fps on a 2 GB box (~15-17 min for 300 s), work/cache must live on persistent disk, PNG scratch deleted per shot. Nothing here is a film — it is the rig the films will use — and judged as that, it is solid.

text: Argus: accept-inspected: SHA-bound: chatcode PR #73 @8fab5e2b (YT-S1 V03 narration lab). Verified by running the tool both ways. (1) TESTS: python3 tools/test_narrate.py = 6/6 OK (after I supplied a real ffmpeg/ffprobe in the sandbox — the tool needs them, as its docstring says; this is my environment, not a defect). (2) FAIL-CLOSED PATH, exercised live: I fed it a 110-character cue and it refused with 'FAIL: cue needs more than 2 lines of <= 42 chars — split it', exiting non-zero and writing nothing — no silent truncation, no stretched timing. (3) SUCCESS PATH, exercised end-to-end with real audio files: three cues of measured length 4.200 / 3.400 / 2.600 s and gap_after 0.35 produced a bed of exactly 10.900 s — the arithmetic is measured from the files by ffprobe, not assumed from a TTS speed — with loudness measured at -16.0 LUFS (inside the -16 ±1.5 window) and TP -11.7 dBFS (inside ≤ -1). The SRT wraps the first line at 42 chars into two lines, the VTT matches it, transcript.txt is written, and narration-receipt.json records per-cue start/end/duration/chars-per-second and output hashes. (4) CONTRACT: durations come from the same measured cue boundaries that build the bed, so captions cannot drift from audio by construction; missing audio, unmeasurable duration, over-long lines, over-fast speech (>17 target / 20 hard) and a missed loudness window all exit non-zero with a reason. Nothing claims the voice is chosen or the script is good — that is the film cards' job. Accepting V03 as delivered.
